notes.calculus-section-17-3-1: Hooke’s law gives k=force/extension. Use m x″+c x′+kx=0 with displacement from equilibrium and the stated initial displacement/velocity; t is in seconds.

notes.calculus-section-17-3-5: Critical damping means c²−4mk=0; using c=14 and k=12 gives m=196/48.
notes.calculus-section-17-3-6: For m=2 kg and k=52 N/m, c=2√(mk)=4√26.
notes.calculus-section-17-3-7: Positive displacement is downward; released above equilibrium means x(0)=−0.1 m. Use the characteristic discriminant c²−4mk to distinguish oscillatory, repeated-root and two-real-root motion.
notes.calculus-section-17-3-8: Use x(0)=0, x′(0)=1. Compare c² with 4mk for each k. Each listed function determines the requested plot; the hand/computer drawing is not automatically assessed.
notes.calculus-section-17-3-9: Substitute A cos(ω₀t) into mx″+mω²x=F₀cos(ω₀t): A m(ω²−ω₀²)=F₀. Add the complementary oscillation.
notes.calculus-section-17-3-10: The forcing overlaps a homogeneous mode, so try At sin(ωt); x″+ω²x contributes 2Aω cos(ωt).
notes.calculus-section-17-3-11: Both phases change by integer multiples of 2π in this time. The stated period need not be the least period if one amplitude vanishes.
notes.calculus-section-17-3-12: Exponential factors never vanish. Solve C₁+C₂t=0 in the critical case and exp[(r₁−r₂)t]=−C₂/C₁ in the overdamped case.

notes.calculus-section-17-3-18: In the stipulated small-angle model θ″+9.8θ=0, use θ(0)=0.2 and θ′(0)=1. The amplitude is √(0.2²+1/9.8), first zero has phase π−atan(0.2√9.8), and crossing speed is amplitude times frequency. This is the linear approximation, not the exact nonlinear pendulum.
